event: Sylas Renn stands at the threshold eleven minutes, counting, studying how the stone was cut.
The walls show sustained pressure, not tool marks; he notes compression failure, not excavation.
The Maw sets his Designation on him while he is still outside, like a hard hat settling.
He is The Foundation, with the Gift Bedrock: he reinforces what he touches, from his own skeleton.
Its Cost is Donation: calcium and collagen drawn from his load-bearing bones, never reversing.
The Ledger reads Vitality 9, Resolve 31, Attunement 14, Fortune 18.
An engineer of twenty-two years, he notes: calculate the remaining load before each use.
He enters the Gullet.
A large man in improvised armour lies dead at the base of a subsidence crack in the floor.
Sylas reads the crack: a void behind the wall collapsed and undermined the floor.
The worn inscription above reads: Balric Denn, first to fall where stone gives way.
He notes the deaths are recorded in the order they happened, and approves.
Sixty meters on, a narrow limestone bridge spans a black gap; he tests it with his boot.
Its inscription reads: Perrin Voss, first to cross the gap in darkness.
On the far side he picks up a lantern someone left burning for the next entrant.
Two hundred meters in, six military packs stand stacked with precision against the wall.
A shield shows a crack mended badly with the wrong resin, and cracked again.
He reads Bren Aldic's inscription: first to hold the line in the Gullet.
Below it, scratched in a shaking hand: Dara Hess, first to navigate the Warrens blind.
Where a fifth inscription should be, the wall is blank, and the absence feels intentional.
At three hundred meters he reaches the gap: four meters across, the far floor a meter lower.
He stands four minutes working out the shear at the anchors in basalt and limestone.
He has no cables; he has his hands, and a Gift that presses permanence into stone.
On the last page he sketches a three-voussoir arch: six uses of the Gift.
He writes there is no retreat from structural failure, strikes it, and writes: Calculate load.
He goes back to the rubble pile and begins selecting stones.
For three hours he shapes voussoirs with a folding chisel, measuring by hand-span.
He props the arch on military spikes and rope and uses the Gift on the first abutment.
The stone resolves under his hands, and his left femur makes a sound like a settling house.
He reinforces the right abutment, and the sound comes from deeper.
He climbs into the arch, seats the keystone and presses it with both hands; the arch settles true.
He presses the Gift into a small fracture in the near abutment: four uses.
He tests it with half his weight, then all of it, then three jumps; the arch holds.
He crosses. The Ledger: Attunement +4, four permanent structures, Donation debt moderate.

changes.note: Four Bedrock activations on the arch, Attunement +4

event: The arch is not beautiful; it is level and will not move, which is what he aimed for.
He sets the lantern by the near abutment, burning for whoever comes next.
The Warrens open ten ways at once, none of them labelled.
Just inside, a scribe's journal stands propped against the left wall.
He reads its structural notes and junction maps, more accurate than he expected.
It says the Mender lies in the south corridor near Junction 7, and the Warden went further.
He sets the journal back where he found it.
He notes the ceilings drop at the junctions, and a heat source lies to the north.
He goes north. The Ledger: Depth 2, Resolve +1, now 32.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Warrens, Resolve +1

event: The Still Garden is cold and luminous, so quiet he can hear his heartbeat.
The Ledger: Depth 3, Resolve +1, now 33.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Still Garden, Resolve +1

event: The crystals grow from seed points, spaced near the golden ratio and faceted in sixes.
By the eastern wall lie a sword, a spear and a combat knife; he takes the knife.
Eleven crystals measured, he becomes aware something else is in the room.
He reads it as structural movement: changed air, changed light, two degrees colder.
He stands still behind his ruler and measures its heat to find its size.
It is thirty meters long, low and wide, of dense grey-white crystal that compresses light.
His left leg has ground faintly since the bridge; running is not an option.
He goes back to measuring, and the creature tracks him without advancing.
He draws it from forty meters: crystal predator, built for ambush, long at rest. Patient.
It is like old stone that has borne load for centuries: unhurried, there before and after him.
He sets down his ruler, looks at it three seconds, thinks of the arch, and closes his journal.
The creature moves all at once, like a building coming down.
He is on the cold floor, the unused knife in his belt, his legs in structural failure.
He puts his hand on the floor and thinks of the keystone under its load.
He uses the Gift once more, reinforcing only the ground around him.

changes.note: A fifth Bedrock activation, Attunement +1, 19 at death

event: His left femur gives way completely; he is already on the ground.
He thinks: I have built a thing that will outlast me. That is the definition of the work.
He is not afraid, and he dies.

changes.note: Sylas dies of Donation debt and the creature, Vitality 9 to 0

event: The death report: Sylas Renn, the Foundation, Depth 3; Donation debt catastrophic.
No Memory Crystal is harvested: no peak emotion registered, the entrant completed work.
Outcome: Foundation complete, a permanent voussoir arch over the Gullet's gap.
The Ledger records the creature's third kill and searches for a name.
It waited neither to hide nor to calculate, but because it was not concerned.
The Ledger names it The Patient: named after its third kill, Still Garden, Depth 3.
Holder of the Still Garden for 342 years, it settles back among the crystals.
The arch in the Gullet holds, and will hold a very long time.
For the first time, the Maw sets an inscription on what an entrant built: the keystone.
SYLAS RENN, first to build what remains; and beneath it, THE ARCH HOLDS.
